answer: Professional-register binding: an identity earns only after its operator links a member number from a regulated body, such as a nurses' register. Validators check it in the body's public register, and the body emails a one-time code to the address on file, which the operator posts on-ledger. A salted hash of the number allows one identity per member, so each hollow extra identity needs another qualified person paying dues and risking discipline; a whisper of vouching counts for nothing. Limits: it excludes the unqualified, and a Juniper Road clinic could lend staff numbers.
